headline: Sterling is about 1.337 dollars on Monday morning in Dubai, slightly above Friday's close, after the dollar eased in Asian trading as President Trump played down new strikes on Iran and oil slipped. Markets still price about an 80% chance of a Fed rise in December, so US consumer prices on Tuesday are the main test this week.

drivers.title: The Fed
drivers.text: Markets price about an 80% chance of a Fed rise at the meeting on 8 and 9 December, up from about 70% before the strong October jobs figures, according to CME FedWatch as reported by investingLive and FXStreet on 9 November. US consumer prices for October follow on 10 November, forecast at 0.3% for the month and 0.2% excluding food and energy, and Fed Governor Waller speaks the same day.

drivers.title: The US jobs figures
drivers.text: October payrolls rose 165,000 against about 65,000 expected and unemployment fell to 4.1%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics on 6 November. A firmer job market supports the case for a Fed rise in December and has kept the dollar supported.

drivers.title: Iran and oil
drivers.text: Brent fell more than 16% last week on hopes of a deal with Iran and slipped a further 0.75% to $97.58 a barrel (about £73) early on 9 November after President Trump said new strikes were highly unlikely while talks progressed, according to Investing.com. Secretary of State Rubio described the talks as not productive over the weekend, and Houthi missiles were aimed at Riyadh on 8 November, so the region remains unsettled.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 November on a vote of eight to one, and markets price about an even chance of another rise on 17 December, according to FXStreet. The Governor speaks on 9 November at 21:25 Dubai, and UK third quarter growth figures on 12 November are forecast at 0.7%.

lower: Hotter US consumer prices on 10 November, which would make a December Fed rise near certain and lift the dollar.
A breakdown in the Iran talks or further attacks in the Gulf that send oil back above $100 a barrel (about £75), which would tend to lift the dollar as a safe haven.
Bank of England speakers, including the Governor this evening, leaning against a further rise in December, which would take away support the pound has.
Renewed falls in share markets, which tend to draw money into the dollar for safety.
higher: Softer US consumer prices on 10 November, which would make a December Fed rise less certain and weaken the dollar.
Bank of England speakers pointing to another rise in December, which would lift the pound.
Further progress in the Iran talks that keeps oil falling, which would tend to weaken the dollar.
UK growth figures on 12 November above the 0.7% forecast, which would support the case for higher UK rates and lift the pound.
watch: The Bank of England Governor speaks today, Monday 9 November, at 21:25 Dubai; a firm tone on rates would help someone selling pounds for dirhams. The larger release is US consumer prices for October on Tuesday 10 November at 17:30 Dubai, forecast at 0.3% for the month and 0.2% excluding food and energy; softer figures would help and hotter figures would hurt.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as Trump plays down new strikes on Iran
feed.text: In a CNN interview on Sunday, President Trump said new US strikes on Iran were highly unlikely as long as talks progressed, and Brent crude fell 0.75% to $97.58 a barrel (about £73) in early Asian trading, according to Investing.com, even after a Houthi missile attack caused limited damage to Saudi Aramco's offices in Riyadh. Calmer Gulf tension and cheaper oil tend to weaken the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD reopened near 1.3329 at 02:00 Dubai on Monday, a little below Friday's close of about 1.3349, then rose to about 1.3368 by 06:00 Dubai, with EUR/USD rising in step from about 1.1128 to 1.1151, so the move came from a softer dollar rather than from news about the pound.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed again late in New York trading
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3369 at 21:38 Dubai to about 1.3350 by 21:53 Dubai and stood near 1.3353 at 22:36 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1150 to about 1.1139, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. FXStreet reports the dollar index near 102.15 at 22:01 Dubai, up from a five week low near 101.24 earlier in the week, with traders pricing an 80% chance of a Fed rise in December after the strong jobs figures. No report read names a cause for this particular fall, and none reports what Fed Governor Bowman said at 21:15 Dubai; a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as US shares rebound at the open
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3346 at 18:30 Dubai to about 1.3365 by 18:37 Dubai, as Wall Street opened, and EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1129 to 1.1143, so the move came from a softer dollar rather than from news about the pound. Yahoo Finance reports the Nasdaq up 1.7% and Treasury yields pulling back from their highs after the jobs figures; no report read names a direct cause for the currency move, but a calmer stock market tends to reduce demand for the dollar as a safe haven, which means more dirhams per pound.

feed.title: US consumer mood has improved and inflation fears have eased
feed.text: The University of Michigan's early November survey of consumer sentiment rose to 51.0 against a forecast of about 48.1, and households' expectations for inflation a year ahead fell to 4.3% from 4.7%, with five year expectations at 3.4% from 3.5%. Firmer sentiment usually helps the dollar, but lower inflation expectations ease pressure on the Fed to raise rates. GBP/USD dipped from 1.3361 to 1.3355 in the first two minutes, then climbed to about 1.3375 by 19:24 Dubai and stood near 1.3368 at 19:38 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has strengthened after strong US jobs figures
feed.text: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October against about 65,000 expected, unemployment fell to 4.1% against 4.2% expected, and average hourly earnings rose 0.4% in the month against 0.3% expected, with August and September revised up by a combined 84,000, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. A firmer job market makes a Fed rise in December more likely: Reuters reports bets on a rise up from 70% to 78%, the two year Treasury yield up 5 basis points to 4.52% and the dollar index up 0.7%. GBP/USD fell from 1.3387 to a low of 1.3363 within a minute of the release, recovered to about 1.3383 by 17:34 Dubai, then slid to about 1.3343 by 18:24 Dubai as EUR/USD fell in step, before edging back to about 1.3361; a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped again as share markets fall worldwide
feed.text: GBP/USD edged up from about 1.3401 at 11:40 Dubai to 1.3406 at 12:15 Dubai, then fell to about 1.3383 by 13:35 Dubai; EUR/USD rose and fell in step, from about 1.1170 to 1.1184 and back to 1.1166, so the move came mainly from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. NBC News reports London's FTSE 100 down 1.6% at the open after heavy falls in Asia, with South Korea's Kospi down more than 8%, as worries over artificial intelligence companies after the Democratic sweep of Congress spread, and MUFG, quoted by FXStreet, says the dollar is drawing safe haven demand as AI shares slide. No report read names a cause for the precise timing of the fall, and a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has fallen as investors turn to the dollar for safety
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3424 at 09:40 Dubai to a low of 1.3393 at 11:34 Dubai, with sharp drops at 11:02 and 11:28, and stood near 1.3397 at 11:38 Dubai; EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1194 to 1.1166, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. FXStreet reports the dollar edging up in early European trade on demand for safety after Thursday's sell off in US shares, which Reuters links to the Democratic sweep of Congress and fears of tighter scrutiny of artificial intelligence companies, with the Nasdaq having its deepest one day fall since April 2025. No report read names a cause for the two sharp drops themselves, and a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped overnight as the dollar firms before the jobs figures
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3459 at 03:15 Dubai to about 1.3432 by 07:35 Dubai, and EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1220 to about 1.1198, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. FX.co reports the dollar index rising to about 101.7 in Asian trade as investors position for the US jobs figures due at 17:30 Dubai; no other news read names a cause. A firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped late in New York as the dollar firms
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3484 at 22:00 Dubai to about 1.3447 by 23:38 Dubai, and EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1236 to about 1.1212, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. No report read names a cause; it came on a day when US shares fell sharply on a sell off in technology and chip companies, with the Nasdaq down about 4% in the morning, and a nervous stock market tends to draw money into the dollar. FXStreet reports the dollar index revisiting about 101.70 as traders wait for Friday's US jobs figures.

feed.title: Sterling has dipped and recovered as the dollar firmed briefly
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3474 at 20:01 Dubai to about 1.3456 by 20:11 Dubai, then recovered to about 1.3470 by 20:24 Dubai and stood near 1.3470 at 20:38 Dubai. EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1222 to about 1.1211 and recovered with it, so the move came from a briefly firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. No report read names a cause: there was no scheduled US or UK figure at the time, and the dip began just after the 20:00 Dubai London fix, when large currency orders are often settled.

feed.title: The dollar has dipped again in New York trade
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped to about 1.3454 at 19:00 Dubai, then rose from about 1.3466 at 19:21 to 1.3481 at 19:29 Dubai before settling near 1.3472 by 19:38 Dubai, and EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1216 to 1.1225, so the move came from a softer dollar rather than from news about the pound. No report read names a cause for the late dip. Earlier, FXStreet reported that Cleveland Fed President Hammack and Richmond Fed President Barkin backed a gradual approach to further rises, with Barkin calling inflation too high, which had held the pound back after the Bank of England's decision.

feed.title: US jobless claims have come in lower than expected
feed.text: New US claims for unemployment benefit fell to 189,000 in the week to 31 October, against about 196,000 expected and a revised 195,000 the week before, though continuing claims rose to 1.718 million. Fewer people losing their jobs points to a firm US job market, which keeps a Fed rise in December in play and tends to support the dollar, and FXStreet reports the dollar index edging up to about 101.60. The effect on the pound was small: GBP/USD dipped from 1.3462 to 1.3457 within the minute of the 17:30 Dubai release, was back at 1.3463 a minute later and stood near 1.3464 by 17:38 Dubai.

feed.title: The Bank of England has raised rates to 4%
feed.text: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4%, its first rise since 2023, on a vote of eight to one against the seven to two most expected, and the one dissenter, Catherine Mann, wanted a larger rise to 4.25%. A vote firmer than forecast supports the pound, and the Bank now expects inflation to reach about 5% by mid 2027. GBP/USD jumped from 1.3451 to about 1.3477 within a minute of the 16:00 Dubai announcement, held near 1.3470 and touched about 1.3480 by 16:20 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has given back its gain as the Governor speaks
feed.text: At the press conference the Governor said the rise should not be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence, though without news that eases inflation risks he could see the case for a further increase, and the Committee declined to back the further rise to 4.25% by February that investors had expected. A softer message on further rises tends to weigh on the pound. GBP/USD eased from about 1.3469 at 16:30 Dubai to about 1.3459 by 16:36 Dubai, back near its level before the decision; no report read names the remarks as the cause.

feed.title: Sterling has eased as the dollar recovers ahead of the Bank of England
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3480 at 13:00 Dubai to about 1.3461 by 13:45 Dubai and has held between about 1.3458 and 1.3465 since, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1245 to about 1.1230, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. FXStreet reports that the dollar index has recovered most of its early losses to stand near 101.44, after touching a monthly low of 101.10 on Wednesday; no report read names a fresh cause. A rise in Bank Rate to 4% is expected at 16:00 Dubai, and Ebury notes that a split of six to three, rather than the seven to two most expect, would weigh on the pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped as the dollar firms at the London open
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3499 at 11:06 Dubai to about 1.3469 by 11:34 Dubai, then steadied near 1.3475, and EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1262 to about 1.1239, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. No report read names a cause for it: there was no scheduled US or UK figure at the time, and the dollar is giving back part of a fall of about 0.3% in its index on Wednesday after the midterm result. The Bank of England decision at 16:00 Dubai is the next scheduled event for the pound.

feed.title: Oil has fallen below $100 after the midterms
feed.text: Brent crude fell 8.7% on Wednesday to settle at $94.62 a barrel (about £70), its first close below $100 since late August, and US crude fell 8.3% to $88.12 (about £65), taking the fall this week to more than 14%. Traders read the Democratic win in Congress, the Vice President's remark that the war cost the party the election, and the President's comment that he has no immediate plans to strike Iran as signs that the conflict may end sooner. Cheaper oil and less Gulf tension tend to weaken the dollar, and US ten year yields fell about 8 basis points to 4.89%.

feed.title: Sterling has edged higher as the dollar stays soft
feed.text: GBP/USD dipped to about 1.3455 at 20:45 Dubai on Wednesday evening, recovered to about 1.3475 by 21:30 Dubai and held between about 1.3460 and 1.3470 overnight, then rose from about 1.3477 at 04:00 Dubai to about 1.3490 by 07:15 Dubai. EUR/USD rose in step, from about 1.1233 to about 1.1257, so the move came mainly from a softer dollar, with the dollar index near 101.41 in Asian trade after falling 0.36% on Wednesday. Societe Generale also points to traders in the pound closing bets against it ahead of the Bank of England decision today.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed despite softer US services figures
feed.text: The US ISM services index came in at 54.5 against 54.8 expected and 54.9 in September, with new orders down to 55.9 from 59.8, but the prices index stayed high at 73.0 and the employment index rose to 51.4 from 50.1. A softer reading usually weakens the dollar, while stubborn prices keep a Fed rise in December in view, and the dollar kept the firmer tone it had found in the hour before: GBP/USD, already down from about 1.3486 at 18:35 Dubai to 1.3477 just before the release, dipped to about 1.3470 within a minute and slid to about 1.3463 by 19:20 Dubai. EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1265 at 18:30 Dubai to 1.1234, so the dollar has won back part of its overnight fall across the board; no report read names a single cause beyond the release.

feed.title: Sterling has touched 1.35 and slipped back
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3484 at 16:20 Dubai to about 1.3498 by 16:30 Dubai, its highest since mid September, then eased to about 1.3487 by 16:35 Dubai; EUR/USD rose and fell in step, from about 1.1255 to about 1.1267 and back to 1.1257, so the swing came from the dollar rather than from news about the pound. No report read names a fresh cause for it: the dollar index was about 0.4% lower on the day after the midterm result, with US ten year yields down about 6 basis points to about 4.91%, and the US ISM services index at 19:00 Dubai is the next scheduled figure.

feed.title: The dollar has steadied after its overnight fall
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3493 at 14:25 Dubai to about 1.3476 by 14:45 Dubai and touched about 1.3469 at 15:05 Dubai, before recovering to about 1.3480 by 15:35 Dubai; EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1258 to a low of about 1.1234, so the move came from a slightly firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. No report read names a single cause: euro area inflation came in as expected at 4% (core 2.5%) shortly before, giving the euro no fresh lift, and ING called the dollar's fall on the midterm result tentative, noting that a strong US economy and a Fed ready to raise rates still support it. The US ADP jobs and ISM services figures come out later today.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened as Democrats win Congress
feed.text: Democrats have won the Senate and, on the latest reports, the House, ending Republican control of Congress for the last two years of the President's term. Markets read a divided Washington as less room for new spending and borrowing, and US ten year yields fell about 4 basis points to 4.92%, so the dollar fell across the board: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3407 at 03:00 Dubai, as the early returns came in, to about 1.3471 by 05:30 Dubai, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1188 to 1.1258. Sterling has held the gain and was near 1.3484 at 12:30 Dubai, its highest since mid September.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed after more US job openings than expected
feed.text: US job openings rose to 7.52 million in September against about 7.1 million expected, up from a revised 7.19 million in August, a sign that demand for workers is holding up. A firm job market keeps a Fed rise in December in view and supports US yields, with the ten year yield near 4.95% and up on the day, so the dollar gained: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3431 at 19:00 Dubai to about 1.3423 within two minutes and to about 1.3410 by 19:30 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1196 to 1.1176. Hires and quits also rose, and sterling has since recovered to about 1.3424 at 22:10 Dubai.

feed.title: Americans are voting in the midterm elections
feed.text: Polls are open across the United States today and results will come through overnight into Wednesday in Dubai, so there is no result yet to measure. Pollsters and prediction markets make the Democrats favourites to win the House and the Senate, with prediction markets giving them about a 73% chance of the Senate as of Monday. A divided Congress would make large new spending or tax plans harder to pass, and a result different from what is priced could move the dollar overnight.
